correctness.rationale: For \(X_A=n^2+2E_A\), \(E_A\) is a finite Fourier series on the independent phase torus. Its constant coefficient is \(\binom n2\). The nonconstant exponent vectors split exhaustively into three-point progression characters with coefficient \(1\) and four-distinct equal-sum characters with coefficient \(2\), together with their conjugates. Orthogonality therefore gives \(\operatorname{Var}(E_A)=2T(A)+8Q(A)\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(X_A)=8T(A)+32Q(A)\). The signed exponent vector prevents unaccounted collisions. The \(B_2\) equivalence follows because every nontrivial pair-sum equality on an ordered integer set has exactly three or four distinct points.

value.rationale: The result identifies an exact, natural second-order statistic for random phase perturbations of sparse Fourier sums. It separates the two genuinely different additive obstruction types with sharp weights and gives a complete rigidity characterization by \(B_2\) supports. This is a structural support theorem rather than a parameter increment, arbitrary slice, or numerical table recomputation.
